title: Which body carries a survey payload furthest per kWh? Hull choice for small autonomous boats
lede: research programme (proposal stage): energy per survey kilometre of hull types for 100 to 500 kg autonomous boats; first sweep: a catamaran out-ranges a monohull in 0.4% of 6,561 friction-limited cases
summary: An open research programme on which body (monohull, catamaran, SWATH, planing hull, hydrofoil, glider, AUV) carries a survey payload furthest per kWh, and where that ranking flips under uncertain drag inputs. Milestone 1 is a stdlib calculator (ITTC 1957 friction line checked analytically, form factor, wetted-area constant, hotel load; 9 tests) and a 6,561-case grid for a 200 kg craft: a catamaran of two slender demi-hulls out-ranges a monohull in 27 cases (0.4%) and in none of the 2,187 equal-length cases; the monohull's best speed is about 1 m/s, set by a 30 W hotel load, with range 560 to 1,188 km as an upper bound. The wave-resistance term is a placeholder and no published resistance curve is reproduced yet, so this is a friction-limited comparison; hull-form constants, efficiencies and water properties are swept or unsourced, and stability and deck area are not modelled. Two DOIs written from memory were wrong and were corrected by the citation check. Preliminary; simulation only.
